subject: Anchoring items manually vs. using multipleGroup vs. linking scores via plink

messages.author: 44edcbbb25378ad9
messages.subject: Anchoring items manually vs. using multipleGroup vs. linking scores via plink
parts:
Hi Phil
First, thanks for the amazing package!

I have data on a language test with four items. Test was administered to finnish and swedish kids separately. I've identified two of the items as anchors in order to make the group scores comparable to each other. I seem to have three alternative approaches to score the response patterns that all lead to different score means between the groups.

1. Manually separate unique items and estimate using single-group mirt
2. Use multipleGroup for estimation
3. Estimate models completely separately and use plink package to scale parameters.

Why do the first two options lead to different results? I would greatly appreciate any insights or guidance on choosing the best alternative. Below is a reprex of what I'm trying to do using the first two methods:

# Load the necessary libraries
library(mirt)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Use the built-in Science dataset
data(Science)

# Split the dataset into two groups
group <- rep(c("Group1", "Group2"), each = 196)

# Estimate IRT model jointly, using two items as anchoring items between groups
mod_multi <- multipleGroup(Science, group = groups,
                           itemtype = "graded",
                           invariance = c("Comfort", "Work", "free_mean", "free_var"),
                           SE = T)

# Estimate IRT model jointly, manually separating non-common items for each group
Science <- cbind(group, Science) %>% mutate(id = 1:392)
Science <- Science %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = c(Future, Benefit)) %>%
  select(-id)

# Joint IRT model
mod_joint <- mirt(Science, itemtype = "graded", SE = T)

# Compare group means
Science %>%
  mutate(fs_multi = fscores(mod_multi),
         fs_joint = fscores(mod_joint),
         group = group) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise_all(mean, na.rm = T)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Anchoring items manually vs. using multipleGroup vs. linking scores via plink
parts:
Hi Ramin,

The multiple group IRT approach treats each group as a sample from a unique population, thereby allowing different properties to be compared across groups if sufficient anchoring is available. So, you'll notice that the latent mean/variance are different in the MG application compared to the standard 0-1 scaling in single group IRT models, which influences Bayes estimates in the fscores() function. If it helps, the single group IRT model is formally equivalent to a MG model when all the item parameters are constrained to be equal across groups (no DIF), and the latent distribution densities are constrained to be equal (e.g., 0-1). Hence, you can think of MG-IRT models as being a blend between the two modeling extremes "ignoring the group membership entirely" and fitting a single group IRT model without group information, and "taking data subsets and fitting single group IRTmodels", which is your 3). HTH.

Phil
